planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; this vigorous tetraploid rewards generous spacing and consistent moisture with its huge, well-branched scapes.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Thomas Tew produces huge, cream-colored blooms with a dramatic black-plum eye and edge above a large chartreuse throat, carried on tall, heavily branched evergreen scapes loaded with buds. Winner of the AHS Don C. Stevens Award for best eyed or banded daylily, it extends bloom over many weeks thanks to its high bud count and rebloom tendency. Divide congested clumps in spring every three to four years to maintain vigor and flower size.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Hotlanta is notably heat tolerant and performs well even in hot-summer gardens.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Hotlanta bears vivid red, waxy-substanced flowers with a large, darker red eye above a green throat, held on well-branched scapes with a high bud count that extend bloom over several weeks. This fragrant, heat-tolerant reblooming cultivar won the AHS Don C. Stevens Award for best eyed or banded daylily. Divide every three to four years in spring as clumps become crowded to keep flowering vigorous.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, average garden soil in full sun; this compact, free-flowering cultivar is an excellent and reliable rebloomer.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; Mister Lucky produces bright orange flowers with a bold, deeper red eyezone above a green throat on compact, early-midseason scapes, and reblooms readily through summer. It won the AHS Don C. Stevens Award for best eyed or banded daylily and is also valued as a breeding parent. Divide every few years in spring to keep clumps vigorous and free-flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; good air circulation helps preserve the delicate petal substance on hot afternoons.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Shimmering Elegance bears large, softly fragrant pink self flowers with a green throat on dormant-type plants that bloom in early midseason with an extended season and rebloom. Winner of the AHS L. Ernest Plouf Award for most fragrant dormant daylily, it is a reliable, mannerly grower suited to mixed perennial borders. Divide every three to four years in spring to maintain bloom quality.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; this evergreen rebloomer appreciates consistent moisture through its extended flowering season.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Chance Encounter produces softly fragrant raspberry-rose blend flowers edged in gold above a small green throat, on evergreen plants that rebloom over an extended season. It won the AHS L. Ernest Plouf Award for most fragrant dormant daylily as well as an Award of Merit. Divide crowded clumps in spring every few years to keep flowering strong.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; tall, sturdy 4-way-branched scapes rarely need staking even when heavily budded.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Mean Green bears fragrant apricot self flowers above an unusually wide chartreuse-to-yellow throat, carried on tall, sturdy, 4-way-branched scapes with a very high bud count from mid to late season. It won the AHS Lenington All-American Award recognizing proven performance across a wide range of climates, along with an Award of Merit. Divide clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain its vigorous bloom display.

common_name: Itsy Bitsy Spider Daylily (Lemon Yellow Spider Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun; this diploid spider form is an early-season bloomer and an easy, reliable grower.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; Itsy Bitsy Spider produces lemon-yellow spider-form flowers with narrow, recurved petals above a green throat, blooming early season on dormant diploid plants. It won the AHS Lenington All-American Award for proven performance across a wide geographic range, a notable distinction for an unusual-form spider daylily. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain flowering vigor.
